subtopics.title: Properties of a parallelogram
subtopics.exposition: A quadrilateral is a closed shape consisting of four straight line segments. A parallelogram is a quadrilateral with both pairs of opposite sides parallel. The interior angles of a quadrilateral add up to 360 degrees. Both pairs of opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal in length. Both pairs of opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal. The diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other. Opposite sides of a parallelogram have equal length. Opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal. To prove the properties of parallelogram ABCD (AB parallel to DC, AD parallel to BC), redraw the diagram and draw the diagonal AC to form two triangles. Use the properties of parallel lines to indicate all equal angles on the diagram before proving the triangles congruent. In the parallelogram proof the equal angles come from alternate angles between parallel lines (A2 = C3 because AB is parallel to DC), and each statement in the proof is given a reason in brackets. Triangles ABC and CDA are shown congruent by AAS (two pairs of alternate angles and the common side AC), so AB = CD and BC = DA. To show angle A equals angle C in a parallelogram, add the two parts of each angle: A = A1 + A2 = C3 + C4 = C, using the equal alternate angles already found. Angle B equals angle D in a parallelogram because triangles ABC and CDA are congruent.

subtopics.title: Proving a parallelogram
subtopics.exposition: A quadrilateral is a parallelogram if both pairs of opposite sides are parallel. A quadrilateral is a parallelogram if both pairs of opposite sides are equal. A quadrilateral is a parallelogram if both pairs of opposite angles are equal. A quadrilateral is a parallelogram if its diagonals bisect each other. A quadrilateral is a parallelogram if one pair of opposite sides are both equal and parallel. To prove that a quadrilateral is a parallelogram, show that any one of the listed conditions on its sides, angles or diagonals holds. To prove that a quadrilateral with both pairs of opposite angles equal is a parallelogram, let the equal angles be x and y and use the sum of the angles in a quadrilateral, 360 degrees. From 2x + 2y = 360 degrees it follows that x + y = 180 degrees, so each pair of adjacent angles (such as W and Z) adds up to 180 degrees. Adjacent angles adding up to 180 degrees are co-interior angles, which shows the lines are parallel (W + Z = 180 degrees gives WX parallel to ZY). Once both pairs of opposite sides are shown parallel, the quadrilateral WXYZ is a parallelogram.

subtopics.title: Rectangle and rhombus proofs
subtopics.exposition: A rectangle is a parallelogram that has all four angles equal to 90 degrees. A rhombus is a parallelogram with all four sides of equal length. A rectangle has all the properties of a parallelogram. The diagonals of a rectangle are equal in length. The diagonals of a rectangle are of equal length (PR = QS). A rhombus has all the properties of a parallelogram. The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other perpendicularly. The diagonals of a rhombus bisect the interior angles. A rhombus has all sides equal in length. The diagonals of a rhombus bisect both pairs of opposite angles. A parallelogram is a rhombus if its diagonals intersect at right angles. A parallelogram is a rhombus if its diagonals bisect the interior angles. To prove the diagonals of rectangle PQRS are equal, show triangles PSR and QRS congruent using PS = QR (opposite sides of a rectangle), the common side SR, and the right angles of the rectangle. To prove the diagonals of rhombus XYZT bisect each other perpendicularly, show triangles XTO and ZTO congruent by SSS, using XT = ZT (sides of a rhombus), the common side TO and XO = OZ (diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other). From the congruent triangles O1 = O4, and since angles on a straight line add up to 180 degrees, O1 = O4 = 90 degrees. To prove the diagonals of a rhombus bisect the interior angles, use the congruent triangles together with alternate angles between parallel sides (X2 = Z1 from the congruent triangles and X2 = Z2 from XT parallel to YZ, so Z1 = Z2). To prove a parallelogram is a rhombus, show any one of the following: all sides are equal in length, the diagonals intersect at right angles, or the diagonals bisect the interior angles.

subtopics.title: Properties of a kite
subtopics.exposition: A kite is a quadrilateral with two pairs of adjacent sides equal. In a kite, one pair of opposite angles are equal (the angles between unequal sides). In a kite, the diagonal between the equal sides bisects the interior angles and is an axis of symmetry. In a kite, the diagonal between the equal sides bisects the other diagonal. The diagonals of a kite intersect at 90 degrees. One pair of opposite angles are equal in a kite (angle ADC equals angle ABC). The diagonal between the equal sides of a kite bisects the two interior angles and is an axis of symmetry. To prove the properties of kite ABCD (AD = AB and CD = CB), show triangles ADC and ABC congruent by SSS, using the two given pairs of equal sides and the common side AC. To prove that diagonal AC bisects angles A and C, use the congruent triangles ADC and ABC: A1 = A2 and C1 = C2.

subtopics.title: Naming special quadrilaterals
subtopics.exposition: A square is a rhombus with all four interior angles equal to 90 degrees. A square is also defined as a rectangle with all four sides equal in length. A trapezium is a quadrilateral with one pair of opposite sides parallel. A square has all the properties of a rhombus. The diagonals of a square are equal in length. The diagonals of a square bisect both pairs of interior opposite angles, so all the angles they make are 45 degrees. To prove a parallelogram is a square, show that it is a rhombus (all four sides of equal length) with interior angles equal to 90 degrees. A trapezium is sometimes called a trapezoid.
